newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products-Prices firmer tracking NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products-Prices firmer tracking NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product prices jumped sharply by late Monday, tracking the strength in the NYMEX futures market.
However, spot market differentials reacted by slipping modestly in mostly quiet activity, according to market traders, as many players streamed to an industry event near San Diego, California.
On the NYMEX, June heating oil rallied 2.13 cents by the close, while June gasoline finished up 1.58 cents.
++ GASOLINE: Differentials showed some weakness Monday, though market players said activity was extremely thin, with no confirmed deals done.
Traders said prompt conventional M1 gasoline was 3.70 to 3.80 cents under the June NYMEX, about 0.10 to 0.15 cent off late Friday levels.
++ DISTILLATE: Little movement emerged from the USG, though some confirmed deals were seen. Prompt heating oil changed hands at 2.10 cents under the June NYMEX, down about 0.20 cent from late Friday.
Prompt low sulphur diesel traded at 1.35 and 1.40 cents under the June NYMEX, at the higher end of the bid-ask range seen late last week, traders said.

++ GASOLINE: Players said the market suffered from a lack of activity, with bids and offers drifting apart at times. Prompt conventional M2 gasoline was talked near 1.50 to 1.75 cents under the June futures near the end of the day, with no deals seen done.
Conventional reformulated A1 gasoline for prompt delivery was seen between about 0.75 and 1.30 cents over the June NYMEX, down about 0.25 cent from late Friday levels.

++ GASOLINE: Midwest traders said differentials on conventional unleaded narrowed slightly to about 2.0 cents above June futures in Chicago and to 4.0 cents over in Group Three, surrendering ground amid resurgent NYMEX futures.
Low sulfur diesel held stable at 6.0 cents over the print in Group Three and eased a smidgen to 4.75 cents over in Chicago, players said.
But activity was very thin in both markets as many traders streamed to an industry event near San Diego, California.
